name: DeerFlow
summary: ByteDance’s MIT super-agent harness (DeerFlow 2.0) with sub-agents, memory, skills, MCP and Docker sandboxes, installed from git rather than PyPI.
description: Vendor-affiliated open project (repo bytedance/deer-flow; not archived; created 2025-05-07; last pushed 2026-11-13; not presented as a brand-new 2026 launch). Vendor: ByteDance. Root LICENSE is MIT (Copyright 2025 Bytedance Ltd. and/or its affiliates; Copyright 2025-2026 DeerFlow Authors). PyPI packages deer-flow and deerflow returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-13; this entry does not invent an installable PyPI name. README: DeerFlow 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite that shares no code with v1; the original deep-research tree is maintained on the main-1.x branch, and active development has moved to 2.0. A README note says version 2 reached #1 on GitHub Trending on 2026-02-28. Documented setup is git clone https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow.git, then make setup, then make docker-init / make docker-start (recommended) or a local make install && make dev. The repo also points coding agents at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bytedance/deer-flow/main/Install.md. Those scripts were not executed. Official site https://deerflow.tech (HTTP 200). The harness is described as built on LangGraph and LangChain, with a filesystem, memory, skills, sandbox-aware execution, sub-agents and MCP. Docker sandboxes can execute commands and manage files — treat them as potentially destructive. A security guide is documented for exposing the app beyond localhost. README promotes BytePlus/Volcengine “Coding Plan” model recommendations and BytePlus InfoQuest (linked as supporting a free online experience). Those are vendor/promotional offers and were not used. Model-API, GPU and hosting costs are separate.

agent_access.notes: No verified PyPI package. Documented setup is git clone plus make setup and Docker or local make install. Install scripts were not run and no model keys were used.
